ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, the perpendicular bisectors $DE$ and $FG$ of $AB$ and $AC$, respectively, intersect $BC$ at points $E$ and $G$. If point $G$ is to the left of point $E$ and $\angle GAE=25^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle BAC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} 
Given that $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, and $FG$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AC$,\\
thus $EA=EB$, $GA=GC$,\\
therefore, $\angle B=\angle BAE$, $\angle C=\angle GAC$,\\
since $\angle B+\angle BAE+\angle GAC+\angle C-\angle GAE=180^\circ$, $\angle GAE=25^\circ$,\\
it follows that $2\angle B+2\angle C-25^\circ=180^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle B+\angle C=102.5^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle BAC=180^\circ-(\angle B+\angle C)=\boxed{77.5^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the base BC of triangle ABC is approximately horizontal, B, G, E, C are on the same straight line and are arranged from left to right in the order B, G, E, C, and point A is above and to the right. There is point D on segment AB; DE is perpendicular to AB and intersects BC at E; there is point F on segment AC; FG is perpendicular to AC and intersects BC at G. In the figure, A is connected to G and E respectively, and ∠GAE is the angle between AG and AE. Reasoning: Let ∠ABC = x, ∠ACB = y. Because E is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, EA = EB, and triangle ABE is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠BAE = ∠ABE = x. Because G is on the perpendicular bisector of AC, GA = GC, and triangle AGC is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠GAC = ∠ACG = y. From the order of the rays in the figure, it can be known that the overlapping part of ∠BAE and ∠GAC is exactly ∠GAE = 25°, so ∠BAC = x + y - 25°. In triangle ABC, ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°, that is, (x + y - 25°) + x + y = 180°. Therefore 2x + 2y = 205°, x + y = 102.5°, so ∠BAC = 180° - 102.5° = 77.5°.
